html:
The Mbabaram were an Aboriginal Australian people of the dry western side of the Atherton Tableland in north Queensland, near today's Mount Garnet.

Their language is famous among linguists. Sound changes had worn its words down, and by chance its word for dog was "dog". R. M. W. Dixon recorded it in the 1960s from its last speakers.

Their neighbours were the rainforest peoples, the Dyirbal, Yidinji and Djabugay, and the Kuku Yalanji to the north. Tin mining around Herberton from 1880 brought miners and cattle into their country.
sum: The Mbabaram were an Aboriginal Australian people of the dry western side of the Atherton Tableland in north Queensland, near today's Mount Garnet.
